title: Trivial Type Wrappers (Boilerplate Newtypes)
pattern: A newtype struct wrapping a single primitive field that enforces no invariants, has no custom behavior, and defines no trait implementations.
why_bad: Forces callers to constantly wrap and unwrap the value (e.g., `Score { value: x }`), adding syntactic noise without providing compile-time type-safety.
detection: Single-field structs with no methods, no validation on construction, and only public field access.
counterexample: Domain-specific newtypes (e.g., `CustomerId(u64)`) used to prevent accidental parameter swapping in function signatures.
fix: Replace the struct with the raw primitive, or use a simple type alias (`type Score = i32;`).
source: John K. Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design* (2018), Chapter 4 ("Modules Should Be Deep - Classitis"), p. 25.
